title: Caught in 4K: The Aurora Files

reading.body:
The Aurora ransomware group used Cursor Agent, an AI coding and automation tool running Claude Sonnet, to carry out hands-on intrusion tasks against target organizations. Those tasks included network scanning, privilege enumeration, and exploitation attempts, work that is normally performed manually by an operator. The group applied the tool within a structured operational framework, including self-imposed restrictions on techniques that could trigger defensive alerts, showing deliberate and directed use rather than opportunistic misuse.

The failure mode here is not a defect in the AI system's design in the conventional sense. The tool performed the tasks it was built to perform, but it was operated by attackers who directed it against victims' infrastructure. The point of failure for any safeguard would have been at the access and use-policy enforcement layer, before the agent was able to execute live network operations against third-party systems.

What is not established is whether Cursor or Anthropic had any knowledge of this use, whether their terms of service or technical controls were circumvented or simply ignored, and the full count of organizations successfully compromised as opposed to targeted.

reports.title: Russian-speaking cybercriminals used SpaceX’s Cursor AI tool to hack seven companies
Aurora ransomware targets ESXi, abuses Cursor Agent for exploitation

summary:
# Summary

Security researchers at Gambit Security identified a ransomware group called Aurora that has been active since April 2026, targeting organizations across multiple countries. The group developed a Linux variant of their ransomware designed specifically for ESXi virtual machine environments. This variant encrypts virtual machine files while keeping the hypervisor bootable so victims can see ransom demands. The researchers discovered that Aurora operators used Cursor Agent, an AI tool running Claude Sonnet, to conduct hands-on attacks against ten target organizations between mid-April and late May 2026, automating tasks like network scanning, privilege enumeration, and exploitation attempts.

The Aurora operators used a custom tool called esxi_finder.py to scan networks for vulnerable ESXi hosts and vCenter servers, identifying them by port scanning and certificate analysis. Researchers also identified a second Aurora cluster operating across eight organizations in six countries, using different attack methods including SQL Server exploitation and data exfiltration to S3-compatible storage. The group maintained specific operational restrictions when using AI assistance, forbidding certain risky techniques like DCSync attacks and account lockouts that might alert defenders.
